lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: proofreading and requesting feedback

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic proofreading and requesting feedback task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a guardian's permission and involvement, the learner shares a draft document with a trusted adult, asks two specific questions about it, listens to the feedback, and makes at least one real revision based on what the adult said.
safetyNotes: The trusted adult who proofreads can be the supervising guardian or another adult the guardian approves in advance.
The learner shares only the document itself and the specific questions being asked, not unrelated personal information.

simulationAlternative.description: If no trusted adult is available to give feedback within the lesson window, the learner instead reads a provided sample draft with planted issues, writes the feedback they would give it as if they were the trusted adult, then revises the sample draft using their own feedback.

materials: learner-local: a draft document (personal statement or another document from the tracker)
adult-or-local: a trusted adult willing to read and discuss it

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Was any part of the feedback hard to hear or hard to act on? What made you decide to use it (or, if you disagreed with a piece of it, what made you decide not to)?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Question specificity: Both warm-up questions target a specific aspect of the draft (e.g., clarity of the opening, whether the ending lands). | Feedback uptake: Revision clearly traces back to specific feedback received. | Reflective honesty: Reflection names a specific reaction to the feedback and explains the reasoning behind accepting or not accepting a piece of it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner ask a second trusted adult (or the same adult a second time, after the revision) whether the specific change addressed their original concern, and record that follow-up response.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic proofreading and requesting feedback task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: proofreading and requesting feedback worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a guardian's permission and involvement, the learner shares a draft document with a trusted adult, asks two specific questions about it, listens to the feedback, and makes at least one real revision based on what the adult said.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact proofreading and requesting feedback decision or action.
Model move 2: Before asking for feedback, write two specific questions you want answered about your draft.
Model move 3: Share the draft with your trusted adult, ask your two questions, and take notes on what they say.

Model check: Question specificity: Both warm-up questions target a specific aspect of the draft (e.g., clarity of the opening, whether the ending lands). | Feedback uptake: Revision clearly traces back to specific feedback received. | Reflective honesty: Reflection names a specific reaction to the feedback and explains the reasoning behind accepting or not accepting a piece of it.

resources.title: proofreading and requesting feedback action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for proofreading and requesting feedback.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: proofreading and requesting feedback coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a guardian's permission and involvement, the learner shares a draft document with a trusted adult, asks two specific questions about it, listens to the feedback, and makes at least one real revision based on what the adult said.
Coach direction: Before asking for feedback, write two specific questions you want answered about your draft.
Learner prompt: Write two specific questions you want your trusted adult to answer about this draft (not just 'is it good?').
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: proofreading and requesting feedback complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Share the draft with your trusted adult, ask your two questions, and take notes on what they say.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I shared the draft with my trusted adult and asked both of my prepared questions.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Summarize the specific feedback your trusted adult gave in response to each of your two questions.

Equal-access rule: If no trusted adult is available to give feedback within the lesson window, the learner instead reads a provided sample draft with planted issues, writes the feedback they would give it as if they were the trusted adult, then revises the sample draft using their own feedback.

resources.title: proofreading and requesting feedback minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was any part of the feedback hard to hear or hard to act on? What made you decide to use it (or, if you disagreed with a piece of it, what made you decide not to)?

Success checks: Question specificity: Both warm-up questions target a specific aspect of the draft (e.g., clarity of the opening, whether the ending lands). | Feedback uptake: Revision clearly traces back to specific feedback received. | Reflective honesty: Reflection names a specific reaction to the feedback and explains the reasoning behind accepting or not accepting a piece of it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: proofreading and requesting feedback supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional proofreading and requesting feedback condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Question specificity: Both warm-up questions target a specific aspect of the draft (e.g., clarity of the opening, whether the ending lands). | Feedback uptake: Revision clearly traces back to specific feedback received. | Reflective honesty: Reflection names a specific reaction to the feedback and explains the reasoning behind accepting or not accepting a piece of it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: With a guardian's permission and involvement, the learner shares a draft document with a trusted adult, asks two specific questions about it, listens to the feedback, and makes at least one real revision based on what the adult said.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Write two specific questions you want your trusted adult to answer about this draft (not just 'is it good?').
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Question specificity: Both warm-up questions target a specific aspect of the draft (e.g., clarity of the opening, whether the ending lands).
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

realRoute.title: proofreading and requesting feedback — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Do not begin the physical action until a household-authorized guardian gives permission and is available for the supervision or review named in this lesson.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Share the draft with your trusted adult, ask your two questions, and take notes on what they say.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record; only the household-authorized guardian attests that the named physical action occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.

retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Question specificity: Both warm-up questions target a specific aspect of the draft (e.g., clarity of the opening, whether the ending lands). | Feedback uptake: Revision clearly traces back to specific feedback received. | Reflective honesty: Reflection names a specific reaction to the feedback and explains the reasoning behind accepting or not accepting a piece of it.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
